description.narrative:
Handicap International/Humanity and Inclusion (HI) har inkommit till Sida med ansökan om stöd om totalt 37 miljoner kronor för ett prjektet "Strenghtening physical rehabilitation services in the North-East of Syria" för perioden maj 2020 till april 2022.
Projektet syftar till att öka tillgången till fysisk rehabilitering och proteser för människor drabbade av konflikt i nordöstra Syrien.
HI arbetar sedan tidigare med sjukhus och hälsomottagningar i tre governorat i nordöstra Syrien (Hasakeh, Raqqa and Der Ezzor) och de kommer att ge 3900 personer skräddarsydda rehabiliteringsprogram som inkluderar bl.a. sjukgymnastik, tillhandahållande av hjälpmedel såsom proteser, psyko-socialt stöd etc. De kommer även att arbeta med familjemedlemmar för att ge dem stöd och öka deras kunskap, utbilda hälsopersonal i fysisk rehabilitering och psyko-socialt stöd samt arbeta med intern och extern remiterring till relevanta instanser.
Sida är den enda givaren till detta projekt och finansierar hela projektkostnaden om 37 miljoner SEK.
Controller har medverkat i bedömning av detta projekt och framtagande av avtal och beslut.

Handicap International/Humanity and Inclusion (HI) has applied for funding for of 37 million SEK for the project Strenghtening physical rehabilitation services in the North-East of Syria during the period May 2020 to April 2022.
The project aims to enhance access to physical rehabilitation and prosthetic for conflict-affected populations through a multi-disciplinary approach.
HI will work with existing rehab units in hospitals and health facilities. They will 1) provide multi-disciplinary rehabilitation services tailored to specific needs of each beneficiary: 3900 patients including for example physio-therapy, prosthetics, psycho-social support, 2) provide education sessions and psycho-social support sessions to caregivers of persons with functional limitations, 3) train Syrian health staff in physical rehab, psycho-social support or prosthetics services and 4) conduct internal and external referrals to relevant services using Gender, Age, Disability (GAD) sensitive elements.
Sida will be the only donor to the project and cover the total project cost: 37 million SEK.

The project aimed to improve the lives of persons with functional limitations in North East Syria by enabling them to gain or re-gain their functional independence through rehabilitation services. The overall objective of the intervention was to improve access to quality physical rehabilitation services that are gender, age and disability (GAD) inclusive. The overall objective was in its turn then divided into three goals:
1) Increasing access: Providing and scaling up physical rehabilitation services in existing rehabilitation units or supporting the setting up of services. Mobile teams were also expected to conduct home visits to beneficiaries when they could not come to the rehabilitation fixed point.
2) Strengthening the health system through close collaboration/capacity building of health facilities and training/coaching of staff members to provide a qualitative and patient-centred service.
3) Community-level inclusion, ensuring that beneficiaries were aware of the services and could access it, that they could provide feedback that would inform improvement and adaptation of the services.
The project targeted vulnerable persons in three governorates in North East Syria. From an activity point of view, focus was on a) activities aimed at strengthening health facilities in their ability to provide quality services and b) activities focusing on reinforcing beneficiaries awareness, participation and feedback on the services.
The project was expected to contribute to a longer term vision of health system strengthening where Syrias national health plan, building on existing structures, would ensure sustainable physical rehabilitation services at three different levels: Specialized rehabilitation services, intermediate rehabilitation services and community level rehabilitation services.

description.narrative:
Introduction
The project has delivered tangible results over the period May 2020 December 2024, with progress in line with the expected targets, and in some areas exceeding initial expectations. Looking across the range of persons reached, among those in need of rehabilitation, caregivers, healthcare staff and referrals to other social services, the total number of beneficiaries reached 16,145. Of these, 34% were men, 46% women, 9% girls and 11% boys.
Increasing access to rehabilitation services
According to the Final Narrative Report May 2020 December 2024, more than 10,700 persons with disabilities and conflict-affected individuals accessed physical rehabilitation, prosthetics and orthotics (P&O), and psychosocial support (PSS). In addition, over 5,300 caregivers received psychosocial support. Functional outcome assessments, introduced from 2021, show that over 90% of patients completing rehabilitation improved their independence, while 99% of caregivers reported reduced burden.
Strengthened health system and partner capacity
HI's reporting highlights that service delivery progressively transitioned to the Kurdish Red Crescent (KRC), thus promoting local ownership. Between 20222024, staff were trained in rehabilitation, prosthetics and orthotics (P&O), psychosocial support (PSS), and Gender-Age-Disability inclusion. The Rehabilitation Management System (RMS), introduced in 2023, improved planning and quality assurance. By the end of 2024, most rehabilitation centers were managed by KRC with HI in a technical support role.
Community-level inclusion
The Final Narrative Report May 2020 December 2024 underlines that 22 persons with disabilities were trained as Inclusion Ambassadors, leading awareness efforts, and that an Organization of Persons with Disabilities (OPD) was formally established in 2023. Feedback and Response Mechanisms (FRM) and community surveys informed adaptations, including adjustments in the scheduling of appointments and the establishment of a child-friendly rehabilitation space in 2024.
Unexpected results
HI's reporting throughout the activity period also includes unexpected results. For example, during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2021) and also during periods of security-related access constraints (2022), HI and its partners showcased their agility and adaptability, finding ways to continue implementation through e.g., tele-rehabilitation and mobile teams. Another example of unexpected results is the fact that the above-mentioned OPD was also recognized by local authorities, providing an institutional platform for advocacy beyond the projects original scope. Furthermore, HI has shared success stories highlighting how rehabilitation of an individual can have broader social impact on families and communities.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
